name: Fernpass
kurzbeschreibung: The Fernpass at an altitude of 1,216 m connects the Inn Valley with the Außerfern: prehistoric rockslide, Blindsee, and the ancient Roman road Via Claudia Augusta.
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig rund um die Uhr geöffnet
beschreibung:
Overview

The Fernpass is a history-steeped Alpine mountain pass at an altitude of 1,216 meters above sea level in the Northern Limestone Alps in the Tyrolean Außerfern. It forms the central road connection between the upper Inn Valley near Nassereith and Imst and the Zwischentoren basin near Lermoos, Ehrwald, and Biberwier in the Reutte district. As one of western Austria's busiest Alpine crossings, the Fernpass links the German Alpine foothills with the Tyrolean Oberland. Framed by the mighty rock massifs of the Mieminger Kette and the Lechtaler Alpen, the pass landscape captivates visitors with its dramatic natural backdrop and emerald-green mountain lakes.

Geology & History

Today's topography of the Fernpass dates back to a gigantic natural event: around 4,000 to 4,100 years ago, the prehistoric Fernpass-Bergsturz broke away from the southern flank of the Wannig massif. Around one billion cubic meters of rock thundered down into the valley, shaping an undulating toma landscape of forested debris hills. The damming of natural watercourses created several idyllic mountain lakes: the deep-blue Blindsee (1,093 m), Mittersee, Weißensee, and Fernsteinsee. Even in antiquity, the Romans recognized the strategic importance of this low mountain saddle: around 46/47 AD, under Emperor Claudius, they expanded the legendary Via Claudia Augusta into the first passable military road between the Po Valley and the Danube. Remains of the historic route with wagon ruts carved into the rock have been preserved to this day. In the late Middle Ages, Duke Sigmund der Münzreiche had the defensive fortifications of Festung Fernstein and the picturesque Schloss Sigmundsburg erected on a rocky island in Fernsteinsee starting in 1462 to control lucrative goods traffic and customs duties.

Visit & Getting There

The Fernpass road (B179) is open and free to drive around the clock, all year round. The entire federal highway requires neither a vignette nor a toll – crossing the pass is therefore completely toll-free (the planned crest tunnel will be completed at the end of the decade at the earliest). In the winter months, winter equipment is legally mandatory. Getting there by car: from the north toll-free from Füssen or Garmisch-Partenkirchen via Reutte and Lermoos on the B179 to the pass summit. From the south via the Inntalautobahn A12 (Mötz or Imst exit) on the B189 via Nassereith up to the pass. By public transport: the VVT regional bus line 150 runs several times a day between Reutte, Nassereith, and Imst/Landeck directly across the Fernpass (stops include Fernpass Hotel Fernau and Fernsteinsee).

Tips

The viewing parking area above the pass hairpins offers a breathtaking photo vantage point overlooking Blindsee and the Zugspitze massif. History enthusiasts can explore the archaeological hiking trail along the Via Claudia Augusta on foot or by mountain bike. The crystal-clear Blindsee is renowned as an eldorado for scuba divers (diving permits and access via Hotel Fernsteinsee). The walking trails along Fernsteinsee and the castle pond are also easily accessible in sections with strollers and wheelchairs.
